must_remember: Stokes' theorem relates a surface integral of the curl of a vector field over an open surface $S$ to the line integral of the vector field around its boundary curve $C$: $\oint_C F \cdot dr = \int_S (\nabla \times F) \cdot n^ ds$.
The orientation of the boundary curve $C$ and the surface normal $n^$ must satisfy the right-hand screw rule.
A force field is conservative if and only if its curl is identically zero everywhere: $\nabla \times F = 0$.
The curl of a vector field represents the infinitesimal rotation or vorticity of the field at a given point.
For any conservative field, the line integral around a closed loop is identically zero, making it path-independent.

glossary.meaning: A theorem connecting surface integrals of curl over an open surface to line integrals around the boundary curve.
A vector operator that describes the infinitesimal rotation of a vector field: $\nabla \times F$.
A vector field whose line integral between two points is independent of the path, equivalent to having zero curl.
The directional convention linking surface normal vector orientation with positive traversal along the boundary curve.
The line integral of a vector field (such as fluid velocity) around a closed curve: $\Gamma = \oint_C v \cdot dr$.
